How this page works

LINE assistant

The assistant for Bella’s LINE Official Account answers only from the approved knowledge and the latest records, and hands the chat to the team when a customer asks for a person. Until Bella’s LINE Official Account is connected, it runs in the LINE simulator only.

What it does not do

  • It does not learn from Bella’s past chats. Nothing customers write is used to train it, and no AI model is connected at all: every reply is a reviewed message, filled in from the approved knowledge and the latest records.
  • It never offers a special or customer-specific price, never diagnoses or advises on treatment, and never promises results.
  • Personal details (appointments, packages, rewards, membership tier) only go to a customer whose LINE is linked to their Bella account, and never into a group chat.

For it to use past chats, Bella would first decide

  1. Which chats or exports may be used, and on what lawful basis. That is Bella’s decision, not O2’s.
  2. What is removed first: names, phone numbers, health details, special prices and one-off arrangements.
  3. That they become draft answers for Bella’s team to review and approve, like the topics below. The assistant never learns from the chats themselves.
  4. How long the source chats are kept, and who may see them.

Each customer’s own history stays in the restricted conversation inbox, never in the assistant’s general knowledge.

The approved knowledge it answers from5 topics

A topic is used only while it is approved, within its valid dates, allowed for LINE answers and approved in the customer’s language. Each language’s status is checked against the assistant’s own rules every time this page opens.

  • A customer’s own appointments, packages, rewards and tier are read only once their LINE is linked to their account.

What it hands to a person

As the chat rules work today.

The customer asks for a person
In any language, or with the “Talk to Bella” button. A task is created for the team with a reply-by time. While the customer waits, the assistant only says they are in the queue and lets them cancel the wait.
A clinical question
Symptoms, reactions or side effects after a treatment, whether a treatment suits someone, medicines or pregnancy, and any medical advice. The assistant never answers it: the chat goes straight to the team at high priority. If the message sounds urgent — trouble breathing or swallowing, severe swelling, bleeding, fainting — the reply first tells the customer to get medical help now or call 1669, and the case is marked urgent.
A complaint, refund or dispute
Including a package balance the customer says is wrong. The assistant does not answer these itself: the chat goes straight to the team.
Automated replies are paused
Every new message waits for a person; the assistant neither answers nor acts for the customer.
A person has taken over
The assistant stays silent and only records the messages.
No approved answer
It says plainly that it cannot answer that yet and offers a person. It never guesses.
A message it does not recognise
It replies with the menu and the button to talk to a person.
A personal question before linking
It asks the customer to sign in or link their account first, and gives no personal details.
An account link that conflicts
It becomes a restricted case for staff to check; nothing personal opens meanwhile.

Special or customer-specific prices

The assistant never offers one: it knows only the public prices in the treatment list. No customer’s special price is in its knowledge.

Clinic manager: lessons

For the Clinic Manager: the team’s day, booking requests, vouchers, completed treatments, package balances, connection problems and stock.

  1. Who does what today
  2. Confirm or decline a booking request
  3. Check a GoWabi voucher
  4. Record a completed treatment
  5. Take over a LINE chat
  6. When a customer questions a package balance
  7. When a connection has a problem
  8. Read the Dashboard
  9. Read the stock book
  10. Receiving, counting and correcting stock (how it will work)

Who does what today

What is this? Today shows who has each piece of work, and which work nobody has yet.

Why it matters: Work with no owner is the work that gets missed.

How to do it

  1. On Today, look for “Unassigned” in each queue.
  2. Agree who takes each item; in a chat, whoever presses “Take over” has it.
  3. In Appointments, the “Needs attention” filter lists what needs someone now: requests, arrivals not checked in, treatments not recorded.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing.

Go to Today

Confirm or decline a booking request

What is this? Some bookings arrive as requests: the customer asks for a time and the clinic decides. A request holds no time until it is approved.

Why it matters: Approving checks the time again, so two customers are never confirmed for the same slot.

How to do it

  1. Open the request from “Pending approvals” on Today, or from Appointments; its status reads “Request awaiting approval”.
  2. Read the line under it: “The requested time is still free right now.” means you can approve now.
  3. Press “Approve request”. If the time has been taken meanwhile, the page offers nearby free times instead.
  4. If the customer wants another time, press “Decline request”, choose the reason, then book the new time with “Book for a customer”.

What saves, sends or publishes: Approving confirms the appointment at once and declining closes the request; the customer sees either in their member area. A customer with a linked LINE account is also sent a LINE message automatically: the booking confirmation, or after a decline a notice that the appointment at that time is cancelled (without your reason), so do not send a second message. Anyone without a linked LINE account is sent nothing: tell them yourself through your usual channel.

In this training workspace: LINE is not connected: these messages are recorded in the LINE simulator and never reach LINE.

Try it: In the training workspace, approve one request and see what its status becomes.

Take careThe customer sees both approvals and declines: check the request in full before you press.

Go to Appointments

Check a GoWabi voucher

What is this? A customer who bought on GoWabi sends the reference; the clinic checks it in GoWabi before any session can be booked.

Why it matters: A voucher can be used once, and only by its buyer or someone they allowed.

How to do it

  1. Open “External voucher checks” on Today and choose the reference.
  2. Check it in GoWabi’s merchant workflow, outside this workspace.
  3. If it is valid, tick “The buyer, or a permitted holder, is this customer”, fill in the sessions and dates as GoWabi shows them and “Where the evidence is kept”, then press “Record the verification”.
  4. If something is missing, use “Ask the customer”; if it is not valid, “Reject this reference” with the reason.

What saves, sends or publishes: Once recorded, the sessions are in the customer’s account straight away and can be booked. A reference you submitted or claimed must be decided by someone else.

Take careWrite down where the evidence is kept, never the evidence itself or a screenshot of the customer’s app.

Go to External voucher checks

Record a completed treatment

What is this? After the treatment, record what was actually performed.

Why it matters: It uses the package session and closes the appointment, so balances stay right.

How to do it

  1. Open the appointment and press “Record completion”.
  2. Check the service performed and the package session that will be used.
  3. Tick “I confirm this service was performed” and confirm.

What saves, sends or publishes: Saved at once, and the appointment is closed. If it uses a package, one session is used and the balance in the customer’s member area changes with it.

Take careA completion is never deleted. A mistake is fixed through a correction someone else reviews, and the original stays in the history.

Go to Appointments

Take over a LINE chat

What is this? When the LINE assistant cannot help, or the customer asks for a person, the chat is handed to the team.

Why it matters: The customer gets one clear answer from one person, and the assistant stops replying while you have the chat.

How to do it

  1. Open Conversations and choose “Needs staff”.
  2. Read why it was handed over (for example “The customer asked for a person”) and whether the chat is “Account linked” or “Not linked”.
  3. Press “Take over”, write your answer and press “Reply”.
  4. When you are done, press “Return to the assistant”, or “Close” if the matter is settled.

What saves, sends or publishes: Once LINE is connected, a reply reaches the customer the moment you press it.

In this training workspace: LINE is not connected: a reply is recorded in the LINE simulator and never reaches LINE.

Try it: In the training workspace, open the LINE simulator, choose a sample member, tap “Talk to staff”, then take the chat over in Conversations.

Take careA chat that is “Not linked” cannot be answered from here, and customers cannot connect their account from LINE until Bella’s LINE Login is set up (writing “Connect account” in LINE tells them so). When such a customer asks for a person, the assistant asks them to contact the clinic directly. Never confirm anything about appointments, packages or prices that are not public to someone you cannot identify.

Go to Conversations

When a customer questions a package balance

What is this? Package balances come from a ledger: every session bought, set aside, used or returned is one entry.

Why it matters: Nobody can type over a balance, so where it came from can always be explained to the customer.

How to do it

  1. Open “Balance disputes” on Today, or the customer’s packages in Membership & benefits.
  2. Go through the package’s history with the customer: when it was bought, how many sessions were used, how many are set aside.
  3. If a correction is needed, the Clinic Manager proposes it with the reason and the Owner approves it. Until that screen arrives, write the case down and pass it to the Owner.

What saves, sends or publishes: A correction is a new entry approved by a second person; the original entries all stay.

Go to Membership & benefits

When a connection has a problem

What is this? Integrations shows each connection to another service, such as LINE, Google Calendar and Sheets, payments and GoWabi, and whether it is working.

Why it matters: A stopped connection can mean appointments missing from the calendar or messages not reaching customers.

How to do it

  1. “Integration issues” on Today lists connections that failed or slowed down.
  2. Open Integrations to see which one, since when, and what to do.
  3. Tell the Owner. O2 support can look only through a time-limited support grant.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing.

Take careNever type a password, key or code from another service into a chat, an e-mail or a note. Bella’s administrator connects each account in Bella’s own account.

Go to Integrations

Read the Dashboard

What is this? The Dashboard brings appointments, customers, income, expenses and the team’s tasks together.

Why it matters: Each figure says what it counts, so everyone decides from the same number.

How to do it

  1. Open Dashboard; the tabs at the top choose the view.
  2. Compare with the period before: the arrow says up or down.
  3. Money (income, payments, expenses) shows only to the Owner and Finance; other roles see counts.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing. When the page shows the “Sample data” line, the figures come from a simulated clinic.

Go to Dashboard

Read the stock book

What is this? Inventory shows what is on hand, what to reorder, lots and expiry dates, every movement, and what each treatment used.

Why it matters: No appointment should go ahead without what it needs, and nothing should be used past its date.

How to do it

  1. “Stock”: on hand against the level to keep; items at their reorder point are marked, and days of cover say how long the rest lasts.
  2. “Lots and expiry”: the lots closest to their date come first; use those first.
  3. “Movements”: every receipt, use and count; a use carries its booking reference.
  4. “Orders” and “Usage by treatment”: what is on order, and what each treatment used.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing. Values and costs show only to the Owner and Finance.

Go to Inventory

Receiving, counting and correcting stock (how it will work)

Not built yet

What is this? When Bella’s live inventory is set up, the team records deliveries, counts and corrections here. The steps below are proposed, for Bella to confirm.

Why it matters: Stock you can trust starts with opening balances Bella approves and every change written down.

How to do it

  1. Setting up: Bella enters each item with its unit, level to keep, reorder point, storage and supplier, then counts once; the Owner approves these opening balances.
  2. Receiving: check the delivery against the order, record each lot and expiry date, and count in the unit the stock book uses (a box of 100 gloves is one box).
  3. Counting: count at each month’s end; a difference is recorded as a new entry with its reason, never typed over.
  4. Using: closing an appointment proposes what the treatment used; the practitioner confirms or corrects it. One appointment is deducted once, however often it is saved.
  5. Reconciling: stock never goes below zero silently; it stops and asks a manager.

What saves, sends or publishes: None of these steps saves anything yet. Automatic deduction stays off until Bella approves real opening balances.

What is measured, and what is not

Integration not connected

  • Measuring starts only once Bella approves it, and counts only visitors who accept it in the site’s cookie choice. Today the website measures nothing at all.

Learning Center

Short lessons by role that take you to the page where the work is done, practice checks in the training workspace, privacy basics, and answers for when you are stuck.

Guide version 1.0 · last reviewed 25 Oct 2026A draft by O2 Design Studio, for Bella to review and confirm lesson by lesson before launch.

Start hereLessons by rolePracticeWhat is samplePrivacy basicsQuestions and glossary
OwnerClinic manager (yours)ReceptionPractitionerMarketingFinance

You can read another role’s lessons, but the pages they lead to open only for roles with the permission.

Practitioner: lessons

For practitioners and clinical reviewers: your appointments, recording treatments, reviewing treatment wording and safety concerns.

  1. Your appointments
  2. Record a completed treatment
  3. Clinical review of treatment wording
  4. What the LINE assistant may say
  5. When a customer raises a safety concern
  6. Receiving, counting and correcting stock (how it will work)

Your appointments

What is this? Today and Appointments show the appointments assigned to you.

Why it matters: You see what your work needs, and no more.

How to do it

  1. Open Today: it says “Showing appointments assigned to you only”.
  2. Open an appointment for the treatment, the time and the instructions the customer sees.
  3. After the treatment, record it (next lesson).

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing.

Go to Today

Record a completed treatment

What is this? After the treatment, record what was actually performed.

Why it matters: It uses the package session and closes the appointment, so balances stay right.

How to do it

  1. Open the appointment and press “Record completion”.
  2. Check the service performed and the package session that will be used.
  3. Tick “I confirm this service was performed” and confirm.

What saves, sends or publishes: Saved at once, and the appointment is closed. If it uses a package, one session is used and the balance in the customer’s member area changes with it.

Take careA completion is never deleted. A mistake is fixed through a correction someone else reviews, and the original stays in the history.

Go to Appointments

Clinical review of treatment wording

What is this? Before a treatment’s text is published, a clinically qualified reviewer checks it.

Why it matters: Customers decide from this text; it must be accurate and promise nothing it cannot.

How to do it

  1. Open “Services: text and prices” and choose a service; texts waiting for review show their status.
  2. Read it as a customer would: no promised result, no diagnosis, no before-and-after claim, no comparison with other clinics.
  3. If it is right, press “Approve: Clinical review”; if not, tell the author what to change.

What saves, sends or publishes: Your approval covers exactly this version. If the text changes later, it needs review again.

Take careThe author of a text cannot approve it.

Go to Services: text and prices

What the LINE assistant may say

What is this? The LINE assistant answers routine questions from topics the clinic has approved.

Why it matters: Customers get quick answers about hours, location and booking, and anything clinical goes to a person.

How to do it

  1. It answers only from approved information, such as hours, location, services, booking and public prices.
  2. It never diagnoses, recommends a treatment for a condition, promises results or quotes a private price.
  3. A question it cannot answer is handed to the team in Conversations.
  4. When you review what it knows, check each answer as you would a published text.

What saves, sends or publishes: Approved knowledge changes what the assistant tells every customer.

Go to LINE assistant

When a customer raises a safety concern

What is this? Sometimes a customer reports a reaction or a worry after a treatment, in a chat or at the counter.

Why it matters: A clinical concern needs a clinically qualified person quickly, not a chat reply.

How to do it

  1. Do not diagnose or advise in a chat. Say a clinician will contact them, and ask how best to reach them.
  2. Tell the clinic’s clinical lead at once, by the route Bella sets, and the Clinic Manager.
  3. If the customer describes an emergency, tell them to call 1669 (Thailand’s emergency medical number).
  4. Write in the record only what care needs.

What saves, sends or publishes: Who is contacted, and how, is Bella’s decision; it is filled in under “Who to ask”.

Receiving, counting and correcting stock (how it will work)

Not built yet

What is this? When Bella’s live inventory is set up, the team records deliveries, counts and corrections here. The steps below are proposed, for Bella to confirm.

Why it matters: Stock you can trust starts with opening balances Bella approves and every change written down.

How to do it

  1. Setting up: Bella enters each item with its unit, level to keep, reorder point, storage and supplier, then counts once; the Owner approves these opening balances.
  2. Receiving: check the delivery against the order, record each lot and expiry date, and count in the unit the stock book uses (a box of 100 gloves is one box).
  3. Counting: count at each month’s end; a difference is recorded as a new entry with its reason, never typed over.
  4. Using: closing an appointment proposes what the treatment used; the practitioner confirms or corrects it. One appointment is deducted once, however often it is saved.
  5. Reconciling: stock never goes below zero silently; it stops and asks a manager.

What saves, sends or publishes: None of these steps saves anything yet. Automatic deduction stays off until Bella approves real opening balances.

Owner: lessons

For the clinic’s system owner: staff access, the information Bella supplies, imports, connections, audit history and approvals.

  1. Who can open what
  2. Bella Setup Center
  3. Bring in Bella’s own records
  4. What leaves the clinic, and where
  5. Audit history

Who can open what

What is this? Staff access lists each role and the permissions it holds; everyone signs in with their own account.

Why it matters: Every page checks the role on the server, so giving the right role is how the clinic keeps records private.

How to do it

  1. Open Staff access and read “Permissions held by each role”.
  2. Give each person the narrowest role that fits their work: a role is a set of permissions, not a rank.
  3. O2 support has an expiry date and no customer records.

What saves, sends or publishes: The page is read-only for now: adding people, changing roles and ending access arrive later. Until then O2 makes the change, and you check it on this page.

Take careWhen someone leaves, their access must end the same day.

Your role cannot open Staff access. If your work needs it, ask the Owner.

Bella Setup Center

What is this? Where Bella supplies and approves its own information: services and prices, hours, policies, connections and the team.

Why it matters: Sample information never goes live: each item stays marked until Bella enters and approves the real one.

How to do it

  1. Open the Bella Setup Center; the required items are listed by group.
  2. Open an item to see what it needs, why, and who decides.
  3. Start with “Services: text and prices”.

What saves, sends or publishes: Entering information saves a draft. An item goes live only after the approvals it needs, in Bella’s live workspace.

Go to Bella Setup Center

Bring in Bella’s own records

What is this? Import the customer list and remaining package balances from the clinic’s own files, inside Bella’s own workspace.

Why it matters: O2 never receives the file; Bella keeps control of its data throughout.

How to do it

  1. In Imports, practise first with the “Practice file (fictional)”; never use real customer data in training.
  2. Save the file as CSV UTF-8, then “Upload and read the file”.
  3. “Match columns”: check which column holds what, then “Save the column match”.
  4. “Check all rows”, fix in the file what is listed, and upload again if needed.
  5. “Review the dry run”: read what the import would do, then “I have reviewed this dry run — approve the import”.

What saves, sends or publishes: Checking and the dry run write nothing. Importing creates customers and balances; it can be rolled back, and a rollback deletes no history.

Take careAn import never gives permission to send customers marketing.

Your role cannot open Imports. If your work needs it, ask the Owner.

What leaves the clinic, and where

What is this? Integrations says, for each connection, what it does and what it may send.

Why it matters: Each connection gets only the data its job needs.

How to do it

  1. Open Integrations and read “Google Calendar”: an entry carries the treatment and booking reference, never the customer’s name or phone.
  2. Read “Google Sheets”: only the columns Bella allows are sent.
  3. Bella’s own administrator connects each account. Never give a password to anyone, O2 included.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing.

Go to Integrations

Audit history

What is this? A record of privileged actions and changes, such as sign-ins, approvals, imports and publications.

Why it matters: When something is questioned, the record shows who did what, and when.

How to do it

  1. Open Audit history.
  2. Filter by kind and look for anything you do not recognise.
  3. Ask the person who did something unfamiliar before concluding it was wrong.

What saves, sends or publishes: The history is read-only: nobody can change or delete an entry.

Go to Audit history

Approvals that need a second person

What is this? Some actions are proposed by one person and approved by another: balance corrections, refunds, published texts and offers, price changes.

Why it matters: Two people on every money or public change protect the customer, the clinic and the person who did the work.

How to do it

  1. Read in full what you approve: the approval covers exactly that version.
  2. Never approve your own work. The system refuses, and asking a colleague to press for you defeats the rule.
  3. Income, payments and expenses are on Dashboard; only the Owner and Finance see money.

What saves, sends or publishes: An approval is recorded with the approver’s name and the time.

Go to Dashboard

Read the Dashboard

What is this? The Dashboard brings appointments, customers, income, expenses and the team’s tasks together.

Why it matters: Each figure says what it counts, so everyone decides from the same number.

How to do it

  1. Open Dashboard; the tabs at the top choose the view.
  2. Compare with the period before: the arrow says up or down.
  3. Money (income, payments, expenses) shows only to the Owner and Finance; other roles see counts.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing. When the page shows the “Sample data” line, the figures come from a simulated clinic.

Go to Dashboard

Read the stock book

What is this? Inventory shows what is on hand, what to reorder, lots and expiry dates, every movement, and what each treatment used.

Why it matters: No appointment should go ahead without what it needs, and nothing should be used past its date.

How to do it

  1. “Stock”: on hand against the level to keep; items at their reorder point are marked, and days of cover say how long the rest lasts.
  2. “Lots and expiry”: the lots closest to their date come first; use those first.
  3. “Movements”: every receipt, use and count; a use carries its booking reference.
  4. “Orders” and “Usage by treatment”: what is on order, and what each treatment used.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing. Values and costs show only to the Owner and Finance.

Go to Inventory

Privacy requests, backups and going live (still to come)

Not built yet

What is this? Tasks that belong to the clinic’s system owner and have no screen yet.

Why it matters: They are named here so nobody assumes they are done.

How to do it

  1. Privacy requests: a customer’s request to see, correct or delete their data comes to the Owner. The screen for it is not built yet.
  2. Backups and recovery: decided with the hosting choice, before launch.
  3. Going live: live data, live messages and live payments are switched on only by Bella’s administrator, item by item, from the Setup Center.
  4. Ending access: until Staff access can be edited here, O2 makes the change and the Owner checks it on that page.
  5. Support grants: O2 support works only through a grant with an expiry and no customer records.

What saves, sends or publishes: None of this can be done from this workspace yet.

Clinic manager: lessons

For the Clinic Manager: the team’s day, booking requests, vouchers, completed treatments, package balances, connection problems and stock.

  1. Who does what today
  2. Confirm or decline a booking request
  3. Check a GoWabi voucher
  4. Record a completed treatment
  5. Take over a LINE chat
  6. When a customer questions a package balance
  7. When a connection has a problem
  8. Read the Dashboard
  9. Read the stock book
  10. Receiving, counting and correcting stock (how it will work)

Who does what today

What is this? Today shows who has each piece of work, and which work nobody has yet.

Why it matters: Work with no owner is the work that gets missed.

How to do it

  1. On Today, look for “Unassigned” in each queue.
  2. Agree who takes each item; in a chat, whoever presses “Take over” has it.
  3. In Appointments, the “Needs attention” filter lists what needs someone now: requests, arrivals not checked in, treatments not recorded.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing.

Go to Today

Confirm or decline a booking request

What is this? Some bookings arrive as requests: the customer asks for a time and the clinic decides. A request holds no time until it is approved.

Why it matters: Approving checks the time again, so two customers are never confirmed for the same slot.

How to do it

  1. Open the request from “Pending approvals” on Today, or from Appointments; its status reads “Request awaiting approval”.
  2. Read the line under it: “The requested time is still free right now.” means you can approve now.
  3. Press “Approve request”. If the time has been taken meanwhile, the page offers nearby free times instead.
  4. If the customer wants another time, press “Decline request”, choose the reason, then book the new time with “Book for a customer”.

What saves, sends or publishes: Approving confirms the appointment at once and declining closes the request; the customer sees either in their member area. A customer with a linked LINE account is also sent a LINE message automatically: the booking confirmation, or after a decline a notice that the appointment at that time is cancelled (without your reason), so do not send a second message. Anyone without a linked LINE account is sent nothing: tell them yourself through your usual channel.

In this training workspace: LINE is not connected: these messages are recorded in the LINE simulator and never reach LINE.

Try it: In the training workspace, approve one request and see what its status becomes.

Take careThe customer sees both approvals and declines: check the request in full before you press.

Go to Appointments

Check a GoWabi voucher

What is this? A customer who bought on GoWabi sends the reference; the clinic checks it in GoWabi before any session can be booked.

Why it matters: A voucher can be used once, and only by its buyer or someone they allowed.

How to do it

  1. Open “External voucher checks” on Today and choose the reference.
  2. Check it in GoWabi’s merchant workflow, outside this workspace.
  3. If it is valid, tick “The buyer, or a permitted holder, is this customer”, fill in the sessions and dates as GoWabi shows them and “Where the evidence is kept”, then press “Record the verification”.
  4. If something is missing, use “Ask the customer”; if it is not valid, “Reject this reference” with the reason.

What saves, sends or publishes: Once recorded, the sessions are in the customer’s account straight away and can be booked. A reference you submitted or claimed must be decided by someone else.

Take careWrite down where the evidence is kept, never the evidence itself or a screenshot of the customer’s app.

Go to External voucher checks

Record a completed treatment

What is this? After the treatment, record what was actually performed.

Why it matters: It uses the package session and closes the appointment, so balances stay right.

How to do it

  1. Open the appointment and press “Record completion”.
  2. Check the service performed and the package session that will be used.
  3. Tick “I confirm this service was performed” and confirm.

What saves, sends or publishes: Saved at once, and the appointment is closed. If it uses a package, one session is used and the balance in the customer’s member area changes with it.

Take careA completion is never deleted. A mistake is fixed through a correction someone else reviews, and the original stays in the history.

Go to Appointments

Take over a LINE chat

What is this? When the LINE assistant cannot help, or the customer asks for a person, the chat is handed to the team.

Why it matters: The customer gets one clear answer from one person, and the assistant stops replying while you have the chat.

How to do it

  1. Open Conversations and choose “Needs staff”.
  2. Read why it was handed over (for example “The customer asked for a person”) and whether the chat is “Account linked” or “Not linked”.
  3. Press “Take over”, write your answer and press “Reply”.
  4. When you are done, press “Return to the assistant”, or “Close” if the matter is settled.

What saves, sends or publishes: Once LINE is connected, a reply reaches the customer the moment you press it.

In this training workspace: LINE is not connected: a reply is recorded in the LINE simulator and never reaches LINE.

Try it: In the training workspace, open the LINE simulator, choose a sample member, tap “Talk to staff”, then take the chat over in Conversations.

Take careA chat that is “Not linked” cannot be answered from here, and customers cannot connect their account from LINE until Bella’s LINE Login is set up (writing “Connect account” in LINE tells them so). When such a customer asks for a person, the assistant asks them to contact the clinic directly. Never confirm anything about appointments, packages or prices that are not public to someone you cannot identify.

Go to Conversations

When a customer questions a package balance

What is this? Package balances come from a ledger: every session bought, set aside, used or returned is one entry.

Why it matters: Nobody can type over a balance, so where it came from can always be explained to the customer.

How to do it

  1. Open “Balance disputes” on Today, or the customer’s packages in Membership & benefits.
  2. Go through the package’s history with the customer: when it was bought, how many sessions were used, how many are set aside.
  3. If a correction is needed, the Clinic Manager proposes it with the reason and the Owner approves it. Until that screen arrives, write the case down and pass it to the Owner.

What saves, sends or publishes: A correction is a new entry approved by a second person; the original entries all stay.

Go to Membership & benefits

When a connection has a problem

What is this? Integrations shows each connection to another service, such as LINE, Google Calendar and Sheets, payments and GoWabi, and whether it is working.

Why it matters: A stopped connection can mean appointments missing from the calendar or messages not reaching customers.

How to do it

  1. “Integration issues” on Today lists connections that failed or slowed down.
  2. Open Integrations to see which one, since when, and what to do.
  3. Tell the Owner. O2 support can look only through a time-limited support grant.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing.

Take careNever type a password, key or code from another service into a chat, an e-mail or a note. Bella’s administrator connects each account in Bella’s own account.

Go to Integrations

Read the Dashboard

What is this? The Dashboard brings appointments, customers, income, expenses and the team’s tasks together.

Why it matters: Each figure says what it counts, so everyone decides from the same number.

How to do it

  1. Open Dashboard; the tabs at the top choose the view.
  2. Compare with the period before: the arrow says up or down.
  3. Money (income, payments, expenses) shows only to the Owner and Finance; other roles see counts.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing. When the page shows the “Sample data” line, the figures come from a simulated clinic.

Go to Dashboard

Read the stock book

What is this? Inventory shows what is on hand, what to reorder, lots and expiry dates, every movement, and what each treatment used.

Why it matters: No appointment should go ahead without what it needs, and nothing should be used past its date.

How to do it

  1. “Stock”: on hand against the level to keep; items at their reorder point are marked, and days of cover say how long the rest lasts.
  2. “Lots and expiry”: the lots closest to their date come first; use those first.
  3. “Movements”: every receipt, use and count; a use carries its booking reference.
  4. “Orders” and “Usage by treatment”: what is on order, and what each treatment used.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing. Values and costs show only to the Owner and Finance.

Go to Inventory

Receiving, counting and correcting stock (how it will work)

Not built yet

What is this? When Bella’s live inventory is set up, the team records deliveries, counts and corrections here. The steps below are proposed, for Bella to confirm.

Why it matters: Stock you can trust starts with opening balances Bella approves and every change written down.

How to do it

  1. Setting up: Bella enters each item with its unit, level to keep, reorder point, storage and supplier, then counts once; the Owner approves these opening balances.
  2. Receiving: check the delivery against the order, record each lot and expiry date, and count in the unit the stock book uses (a box of 100 gloves is one box).
  3. Counting: count at each month’s end; a difference is recorded as a new entry with its reason, never typed over.
  4. Using: closing an appointment proposes what the treatment used; the practitioner confirms or corrects it. One appointment is deducted once, however often it is saved.
  5. Reconciling: stock never goes below zero silently; it stops and asks a manager.

What saves, sends or publishes: None of these steps saves anything yet. Automatic deduction stays off until Bella approves real opening balances.

Go to Inventory

The basics for Bella’s team; not legal advice. The clinic’s policy and Bella’s advisers set the details.

Whose data this is

  • A customer’s personal data belongs to the customer. Bella is responsible for it under Thailand’s Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019), the PDPA.
  • Health and treatment information is sensitive data, held to stricter rules.

Only what you need

  • Open only the records your task needs; your role already hides what your work does not need.
  • Never look up people you know out of curiosity.
  • Write in a record only what care needs.

Never in a chat

  • Never type or send health details, photos of skin or treated areas, ID card numbers, card numbers or passwords by LINE, e-mail, social media messages or any AI tool outside this workspace.
  • In a chat, say only what booking needs, and never quote a price that is not public: a member’s benefit is shown to that member in their own member area.

Marketing needs permission

  • Send promotions only to customers who agreed.
  • An import never creates permission, and a customer who said no stays a no.

Screens and exports

  • Do not photograph or screenshot customer screens, or move customer lists to personal devices.
  • Lock your screen when you step away.
  • Your account is yours alone; never let anyone else use it. O2 will never ask for your password.

When something goes wrong

  • If you sent something to the wrong person, put private information in the wrong place or lost a device, tell the Owner at once; do not fix it quietly.
  • The PDPA requires the clinic to notify the Personal Data Protection Committee’s office within 72 hours when a breach may put people at risk, so minutes count.

Customers’ requests

  • If a customer asks to see, correct or delete their data, or to stop messages, note the request and pass it to the Owner the same day.
  • Do not refuse or promise anything yourself.

When you are stuck

A page says my role doesn’t include it
Your role lacks the permission that page needs; it is checked on the server. If your work needs it, ask the Owner to add the permission to your role.
I pressed approve, but the time is no longer free
Someone booked that time meanwhile. Offer the customer one of the nearby free times shown, then decline the request and book the new time.
I cannot reply in a chat
Take the chat over first. A chat not linked to an account cannot be answered from this page, and linking from LINE opens once Bella’s LINE Login is set up. Until then the assistant asks a customer who wants a person to contact the clinic directly. In this training workspace LINE is not connected, so replies are recorded in the LINE simulator.
A customer says their package balance is wrong
Do not change the number yourself. Go through the package’s history with them; if it still does not match, pass it to the Clinic Manager to propose a correction for the Owner to approve.
The same GoWabi reference was submitted twice
Decide the competing claims first; the page will not record a verification until they are decided.
The Thai in my import file is garbled
Save the file from Excel as “CSV UTF-8” and upload it again.
The year in my file is 2569
Use the Gregorian year, such as 2026. Buddhist-Era years are not converted silently, so no date can shift unnoticed.
I published, but the live website did not change
In the training workspace, publishing changes this preview only. Text goes live only when Bella’s staff approve it in the live workspace.
Why can’t I see any money figures?
Money shows only to the Owner and Finance; other roles see counts.
The stock numbers look odd
Inventory shows a simulated clinic for now. Once Bella’s live inventory is set up, the numbers come from Bella’s own deliveries and counts.
I typed private information into a chat by mistake
Tell the Owner at once; do not forward it or delete it quietly. See Privacy basics.

Who to ask

Bella fills in names and numbers before launch, so no one is named here yet.

A page says your role doesn’t include it, or a role needs changing
The Owner (who manages staff access)
A connection or the system has a problem
The Clinic Manager first, then the Owner; O2 support helps only under a time-limited grant
A customer’s health or safety concern
The clinical lead Bella names, and the Clinic Manager
Personal data leaked or sent to the wrong person
The Owner, at once
A package balance or voucher does not match
The Clinic Manager
Payments or refunds
Finance

Glossary

Request awaiting approval
A booking the customer asked for that holds no time and is not yet a confirmed appointment.
Time held
A time kept for a customer briefly while they book; released if they do not confirm in time.
Check-in
The record that a customer has arrived; not the treatment or the payment.
Completion
The record that a treatment was performed; it uses the package session and closes the appointment.
Package session
One of the sessions a customer bought in advance; each use, hold or return is one ledger entry.
Handoff
When the LINE assistant passes a chat to the team.
Take over
Taking a chat on yourself; the assistant stops replying until you give it back.
Linked account
A LINE chat tied to a verified customer account, so you know who it is.
Level to keep
What an order tops stock up to.
Reorder point
At or below this many, more is ordered.
Lot
Stock received together with one expiry date.
Days of cover
Stock on hand divided by the daily use of the last 30 days.
Dry run
A view of what an import would do, written nowhere.
Allow-list
The columns Bella allows to be sent to a spreadsheet; nothing else is sent.
Training workspace
A workspace with fictional records only, for practice; nothing leaves it.
Separation of duties
The person who proposes or writes is never the one who approves.
PDPA
Thailand’s Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019), which protects personal data.

Reception: lessons

For Reception: finding customers, checking who they are, appointment statuses, rescheduling, arrivals and LINE chats handed to the team.

  1. Start the day on Today
  2. Confirm or decline a booking request
  3. Book for a customer, and check who they are
  4. Reschedule without losing the original
  5. Arrivals and missed appointments
  6. Take over a LINE chat

Start the day on Today

What is this? Today gathers the work waiting for the team: today’s appointments, requests to approve, LINE chats handed to staff, vouchers to check and more.

Why it matters: Each count is taken from the list under it, so nothing waiting is missed and no two people do the same job.

How to do it

  1. Open “Today” in the menu.
  2. Read each queue’s count; if you are unsure what it counts, open “What counts here”.
  3. Start with “Pending approvals” and “Unresolved handoffs”: a customer is waiting on both.
  4. Open an item to go straight to the page where it is handled.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing. Queues your role may not see are left out.

Try it: In the training workspace, open one item from every queue that has work, and see where each one takes you.

Go to Today

Confirm or decline a booking request

What is this? Some bookings arrive as requests: the customer asks for a time and the clinic decides. A request holds no time until it is approved.

Why it matters: Approving checks the time again, so two customers are never confirmed for the same slot.

How to do it

  1. Open the request from “Pending approvals” on Today, or from Appointments; its status reads “Request awaiting approval”.
  2. Read the line under it: “The requested time is still free right now.” means you can approve now.
  3. Press “Approve request”. If the time has been taken meanwhile, the page offers nearby free times instead.
  4. If the customer wants another time, press “Decline request”, choose the reason, then book the new time with “Book for a customer”.

What saves, sends or publishes: Approving confirms the appointment at once and declining closes the request; the customer sees either in their member area. A customer with a linked LINE account is also sent a LINE message automatically: the booking confirmation, or after a decline a notice that the appointment at that time is cancelled (without your reason), so do not send a second message. Anyone without a linked LINE account is sent nothing: tell them yourself through your usual channel.

In this training workspace: LINE is not connected: these messages are recorded in the LINE simulator and never reach LINE.

Try it: In the training workspace, approve one request and see what its status becomes.

Take careThe customer sees both approvals and declines: check the request in full before you press.

Go to Appointments

Book for a customer, and check who they are

What is this? Book on a customer’s behalf at the counter or on the phone, with the same rules as online booking.

Why it matters: The website, the member area and the counter use one booking service, so free times and packages always agree.

How to do it

  1. Go to Appointments and press “Book for a customer”.
  2. Find the customer by name, phone number or booking reference. If more than one record could match, ask for something only that customer would know before choosing.
  3. See whether each contact detail is “Identity verified” or “Not yet verified”, and use only verified ones.
  4. Choose the treatment, payment and time, go to “Review and book”, read it back to the customer, then press “Book and confirm”.

What saves, sends or publishes: The appointment is saved at once and holds the practitioner and room. Some treatments are saved as a request awaiting approval instead.

Take careNever book under a record you are not sure is this customer’s: a wrong match shows one person’s appointments and packages to another.

Go to Book for a customer

Reschedule without losing the original

What is this? Move an appointment to another free time.

Why it matters: The current appointment stays until the new time is confirmed, so a change that fails never leaves the customer with nothing.

How to do it

  1. Open the appointment in Appointments and press “Reschedule”.
  2. Choose the new date: only times free under the same rules as online booking are shown, preparation and cleanup included.
  3. Choose the time and confirm. A package session set aside moves with the appointment.
  4. Open “History” in the appointment: it shows the old time and the new one.

What saves, sends or publishes: The change is saved at once. Once Bella’s calendar is connected, it shows the new time with the treatment and booking reference only, never the customer’s name. A customer with a linked LINE account is also sent the new date and time by LINE automatically, and their reminders move to the new time, so do not send a second message. Anyone without a linked LINE account is sent nothing: tell them yourself through your usual channel.

In this training workspace: LINE is not connected: the message with the new time is recorded in the LINE simulator and never reaches LINE.

Take careThe customer sees the new time in their member area.

Go to Appointments

Arrivals and missed appointments

What is this? Record that a customer has arrived, and find appointments nobody has closed.

Why it matters: Arrival, treatment and payment are separate records, each made once by the person who saw it.

How to do it

  1. On the day, when the customer arrives, open the appointment and press “Check in”. It records the arrival only, not the treatment or the payment.
  2. After its end time, an appointment nobody closed appears in “Missing completion records” on Today.
  3. There is no button for a missed appointment yet: if the customer did not come, tell the Clinic Manager, who notes it until that screen arrives.
  4. Never cancel and book again instead: that leaves a record that is not true, and a customer with a linked LINE account is sent a cancellation notice.

What saves, sends or publishes: Check-in is saved at once and shows on Today.

Go to Appointments

Take over a LINE chat

What is this? When the LINE assistant cannot help, or the customer asks for a person, the chat is handed to the team.

Why it matters: The customer gets one clear answer from one person, and the assistant stops replying while you have the chat.

How to do it

  1. Open Conversations and choose “Needs staff”.
  2. Read why it was handed over (for example “The customer asked for a person”) and whether the chat is “Account linked” or “Not linked”.
  3. Press “Take over”, write your answer and press “Reply”.
  4. When you are done, press “Return to the assistant”, or “Close” if the matter is settled.

What saves, sends or publishes: Once LINE is connected, a reply reaches the customer the moment you press it.

In this training workspace: LINE is not connected: a reply is recorded in the LINE simulator and never reaches LINE.

Try it: In the training workspace, open the LINE simulator, choose a sample member, tap “Talk to staff”, then take the chat over in Conversations.

Take careA chat that is “Not linked” cannot be answered from here, and customers cannot connect their account from LINE until Bella’s LINE Login is set up (writing “Connect account” in LINE tells them so). When such a customer asks for a person, the assistant asks them to contact the clinic directly. Never confirm anything about appointments, packages or prices that are not public to someone you cannot identify.

Go to Conversations

For Marketing: service texts, approval and publication, pictures, promotions, search and reading the figures.

Edit a service’s text

What is this? Each service has a name, a short description and details, in Thai, English and Chinese.

Why it matters: Customers choose from this text on the website and in the member area.

How to do it

  1. Open “Services: text and prices” and choose the service and the language.
  2. Write the Thai first; the English and Chinese are written for their own readers, not translated word for word.
  3. Press “Save draft”. A draft is never shown to customers.
  4. When it is ready, press “Send for review”.

What saves, sends or publishes: Saving keeps a draft; sending for review reaches the approvers. Nothing is public yet.

Go to Services: text and prices

Approval first, then publication

What is this? A text goes live only once it has every approval it needs.

Why it matters: Everything a customer reads is read by two people first.

How to do it

  1. Approvers read the text and record their approval: each translation needs a “Translation review”, and treatment wording a clinical review.
  2. The author of a text cannot approve it.
  3. When every approval is in, use “View the page on the website” first, then press “Publish”.

What saves, sends or publishes: Publishing changes the website and the member area at once.

In this training workspace: Publishing changes this training workspace only, never Bella’s live website.

Take careEvery customer sees what is published.

Go to Services: text and prices

Pictures

What is this? Photographs on the website and in posts.

Why it matters: A picture tells customers what the clinic is like, so it must be true.

How to do it

  1. Use only photographs Bella owns or has permission to use.
  2. Never present a stock photo as Bella’s clinic, team or customers.
  3. Before-and-after pictures need the customer’s written consent and the clinic’s approval before every use.
  4. Never use a photo in which a customer can be recognised without their consent.

What saves, sends or publishes: A picture is public only after the approval Bella sets for it.

Your role cannot open Website editor. If your work needs it, ask the Owner.

Promotions and prices

What is this? An offer has a price, conditions, a start date, an end date, and who may use it.

Why it matters: A wrong or expired price costs the clinic money and the customer’s trust.

How to do it

  1. Draft the offer with its conditions and dates; someone with approval permission publishes it.
  2. Keep the kinds of price apart: the public price, an approved public promotion, a member’s benefit shown only to that member, and a private price that is never published.
  3. Every offer has an end date.
  4. Health promotions, and anything clinical, also need a clinical review.

What saves, sends or publishes: Once published, customers see the offer at once.

Go to Growth & content

Search, and reading the figures

What is this? Every page has a title and a description in each language, which search engines show.

Why it matters: Clear, true titles bring the right customers.

How to do it

  1. Write titles and descriptions for people, in each language: what the service is, and where.
  2. Never promise results or claim to be the best.
  3. Read Growth & content for new customers, return rate and channels; compare periods, not single days.
  4. Nobody can guarantee a search ranking.

What saves, sends or publishes: Changed titles reach search engines only after publication, and take time to show.

Go to Growth & content

Read the Dashboard

What is this? The Dashboard brings appointments, customers, income, expenses and the team’s tasks together.

Why it matters: Each figure says what it counts, so everyone decides from the same number.

How to do it

  1. Open Dashboard; the tabs at the top choose the view.
  2. Compare with the period before: the arrow says up or down.
  3. Money (income, payments, expenses) shows only to the Owner and Finance; other roles see counts.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing. When the page shows the “Sample data” line, the figures come from a simulated clinic.

Go to Dashboard

Reconcile each day

What is this? For every closed day: what was recorded against what reached the bank, by payment method.

Why it matters: A difference found the next day is easy to explain; a month later it is not.

How to do it

  1. Open Reconciliation.
  2. Start with the items to look at; each one says what to do.
  3. Check one method at a time: card batches arrive a few days later, GoWabi pays out on its own schedule.

What saves, sends or publishes: Reading changes nothing. When the page shows the “Sample data” line, the figures come from a simulated clinic.

Your role cannot open Reconciliation. If your work needs it, ask the Owner.

Refunds (how it will work)

Not built yet

What is this? Money returned to a customer.

Why it matters: A refund moves money out, so it needs two people and a written reason.

How to do it

  1. Finance prepares the refund with the reason and the original payment.
  2. The Owner approves it; whoever prepared it cannot approve it.
  3. The refund is recorded as its own entry; the original payment stays in the history.

What saves, sends or publishes: The customer is told through the clinic’s usual channel.

What is this? Inventory shows what is on hand, what to reorder, lots and expiry dates, every movement, and what each treatment used.

Service name
Anti-wrinkle injection (forehead and frown lines)
Short description
A prescription-medicine injection for expression lines, planned with the doctor at your appointment.
What it involves
The doctor looks at the muscles and lines as you make expressions, explains the areas and amount that suit you, then injects with a very fine needle. About 30 minutes in the room.
Preparation
Tell the doctor about any medication, previous injections, and pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid strenuous exercise on the day.
Who it suits
Whether this treatment suits you is assessed by the clinic’s doctor at your appointment. This page is general information, not personal advice.

How wording on the website changes

  1. Change the wording and save it as a draft. Customers do not see it yet.
  2. Look at the preview, then send it for review.
  3. Someone else checks and approves it. Nobody approves their own wording, and an approval covers exactly the text that was checked: a change after approval needs a new approval.
  4. A person who may publish presses Publish. The website changes at once.
  5. Every version is kept in the history; a version that was live before can be brought back.
